chapters.title: Memory, notes and what it knows
chapters.label: Intro

beats.text: Tell your assistant something {once}once, and it {remembers}remembers. Give it your {documents}documents, and it {answers}answers from them.
Today: {memory}memory and notes, {knows}what it knows, and {drop}dropping files on it.

In {settings}Settings, Memory, is what the assistants {know}know about you, shared by all of them. With {learn}Learn from what you talk about, after each chat they note what's worth remembering: your name, what you like, important dates.
Or tell them: {remember}remember that I'm allergic to seafood. Ask {what}what do you remember about me, or say {forget}forget that. And here you can {edit}edit or delete anything.
{notes}Notes are different: they're what you ask them to note down. Say {say}note that, call the landlord, and it's there for later.
In {knows}What it knows, {add}add folders or files: notes, manuals, contracts, invoices. They're {read}read once, on this PC, and it keeps an eye on them. {nothing}Nothing leaves it.
Turn on {pictures}Read pictures and scanned PDFs, and it reads those too, with Windows' text recognition.
Then ask: {ask}how much was the electricity bill in October? It answers with {answers}what your documents say, and tells you {where}where it comes from. {try}Try a search shows what it would find.

One last tip: {drag}drag a file onto an assistant. It asks {what}what to do with it: {inside}what's inside, {summarize}summarize, or {read}read it to you. With a picture, {describe}what is it. Or just {tell}tell it.
Next up: {next}the assistant's voice and personality.
